meanings: adjective: ready or helpful when needed (used with "not" to describe problems)
examples: Although our education system is suffering badly from a lack of money, help from the government hasn't been forthcoming.

meanings: verb: to give abilities to
examples: The author James Joyce endowed the character Leopold Bloom with patience, humility, and tolerance.

meanings: adjective: very complicated, with many parts (used for abstract things)
examples: Katie was surprised that the process for learning how to code was not nearly as involved as she had anticipated.

meanings: verb: to grow or spread extremely quickly
examples: Since the invention of the smartphone, internet access across the world has mushroomed.

meanings: adjective: violent and uncontrolled
examples: Some see the great white shark as a savage animal with a thirst for blood, but as a biologist, I know they are only doing what they must to survive.

meanings: verb: to want something badly and immediately
examples: I enjoy coffee once in a while, but my friend craves it: he can't even imagine going a day without it!

meanings: verb: replace someone or something that doesn't fill a role anymore
examples: As researchers build better robots, we should worry about being supplanted by machines that can do the same things we are paid to do.

meanings: noun: a container
examples: Two-thousand-year-old pots found in Iraq, known as "Baghdad batteries," were probably not actually batteries but instead vessels for important texts.

meanings: noun: an enjoyable smell
examples: As the pie came out of the oven, the aroma of baked apples filled the room.

meanings: adjective: impossible to stop
examples: As summer nears its end, brown bears eat as much as possible to prepare for the inexorable coming of winter.

meanings: verb: to flow very slowly
examples: I watched the raindrop trickle down the car window as we sat stopped at a stoplight.

meanings: verb: to remove something unwanted from a group
examples: Because we had 67 applications for the 20 positions on the committee, we began by culling all who clearly lacked even the minimum experience.

meanings: noun: confidence and enthusiasm within a group of people
examples: The company morale at Yahoo has suffered because of the frequent changes of CEOs.

meanings: adjective: mysterious and scary
examples: As Joel walked through the haunted house, the eerie music made him even more scared than he already was.

meanings: noun: serious danger
examples: Politicians who warn about the great perils we face from other countries will always get attention, even when their warnings aren't based on facts.

meanings: adjective: happening often without stopping (used for bad things)
examples: Now that they are building a skyscraper next door, the sound of construction is incessant and impossible to escape.

meanings: noun: an untruthful reason given for an action
examples: As the movie started, Karthik moved slowly closer to Sofia under the pretext of getting more comfortable in his seat.

meanings: noun: the highest point
examples: Top athletes in most sports hit the apexes of their careers in their 20s or early 30s, after which health becomes harder to maintain.

meanings: adjective: depressing, hopeless; very bad
examples: The month after I lost my job was dismal; I couldn't find work, so I was afraid of not being able to pay rent or buy food.

meanings: noun: the visual objects and signs associated with a position or status
examples: After receiving a meat thermometer as a gift, I realized I was becoming surrounded by the trappings of adulthood.

meanings: noun: something that starts or speeds up an event
examples: The death of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, the man who was next in line to rule the Austro-Hungarian Empire, was the catalyst for World War I.

meanings: adjective: willing to be bold in social situations or to take risks
examples: In my first week of teaching preschool, one especially audacious child tried to cut my hair without even asking.

meanings: verb: to stick to and not come off
examples: A fly's feet adhere to most surfaces, giving it the ability to walk upside-down on a ceiling.

meanings: adjective: easy to understand; from clear thinking
examples: My physics teacher made complex models easy to understand by explaining them with lucid, concrete examples that we could relate to.

meanings: noun: one side or aspect (used for abstract things)
examples: After two years of living abroad, Mario decided that he missed some facets of American food culture, including the variety of restaurant types.

meanings: adjective: unclear
examples: A typical ten-year-old has only a hazy idea of how to manage money and how important it is to do so.

meanings: verb: to press down; to cause to drop
examples: A rise in unemployment typically depresses the stock market, because few want to invest in companies that cannot employ people.

meanings: verb: to keep a tradition
examples: Thousands of years after the earth was first proved to be a sphere, some groups today uphold the belief that our planet is actually flat.

meanings: adjective: highest in rank or importance
examples: Regardless of what people think of Michael Jackson today, he was one of the foremost musicians of his time.

meanings: verb: to lead a change
examples: After volunteering at a homeless shelter, I decided to spearhead a volunteer program at my office to get more of my coworkers involved.

meanings: verb: to attack without pausing
examples: Early in World War II, the US rarely attacked Japan's home islands, but after the fall of Okinawa, the Air Force bombarded Japan for months.

meanings: verb: to trade in a system that doesn't use money
examples: Because she couldn't afford my tutoring prices, she suggested bartering: she gave me an hour massage for each hour of tutoring.

meanings: noun: a force pushing forward
examples: I've always been confused by the source of propulsion of giant cargo ships—how can they efficiently move so much weight?

meanings: verb: to completely destroy (used for buildings)
examples: The armies of the north poured quickly into the south, stealing food and valuables, setting fires to homes, and razing entire towns.

meanings: verb: to clarify by making less general
examples: Patrick qualified his love for San Francisco, adding that he didn't like the weather as much as the weather in Los Angeles.

meanings: adjective: extremely difficult and tiring
examples: When my father turned 60, he took a surprising interest in grueling races, sometimes running 150 kilometers in the summer heat.

meanings: adjective: lasting for a very short time
examples: Roller coasters are thrilling, but the experience is fleeting; most rides take under 90 seconds to complete.

meanings: verb: to pull back
examples: My pet snail hates me! Every time I try to touch him he retracts his head.

meanings: verb: to hide when preparing to attack
examples: Toshio sat quietly in his small boat, terrified of the crocodiles that lurked in the water below.

meanings: verb: to throw forcefully
examples: Most people simply drop their pennies in the wishing well, but Jim would insist on hurling his coins into the well, producing a big splash.

meanings: noun: a natural ability for a specific skill
examples: I have a knack for remembering faces, but I have a lot of trouble remembering names.

meanings: adjective: suspicious and possibly wrong
examples: I saw a carton of milk with an expiration date so dubious I decided to buy it for fun: it has a date one year from today printed on it.

meanings: preposition: in spite of
examples: High prices notwithstanding, over 70 million iPhones were sold in the last three months.

meanings: adjective: well combined into one whole
examples: A well-written, cohesive essay will keep on topic at all times, never losing sight of the main argument.

meanings: verb: to produce eggs (used for fish, frogs, etc.)
examples: Salmon begin their lives in streams, then swim out to the ocean to spend their lives, but return to the same streams to spawn.

meanings: verb: to become much less or many fewer
examples: Due to repeated overfishing, the numbers of snow crabs have severely dwindled in recent years.

meanings: verb: to melt slowly after a temperature change
examples: The ice cream was really hard to scoop, so I left it on the counter to thaw for 30 minutes.

meanings: verb: to encourage or stimulate
examples: In an unwise attempt to spur more intense conversation among his students, Professor Greene assigned a clearly racist text for reading.

meanings: verb: to make worse
examples: The soccer field is already muddy and unfit for play, and another few days of rain will exacerbate the problem even further.

meanings: verb: to fail to notice
examples: Although she played perfectly throughout the game, Michelle was overlooked in the celebration of her volleyball team's victory.
